The disease is most… 2496002 familial-amyloidotic-polyneuropathy:-current-and-emerging-treatment-options-for-transthyretin-mediated-amyloidosis familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy current emerging treatment options transthyretin Transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy (TTR-FAP) is a fatal clinical disorder Familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy: current and emerging treatment options for transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis Transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy (TTR-FAP) is a fatal clinical disorder characterized by extracellular deposition of abnormal fibrils derived from misfolded, normally soluble transthyretin (TTR) molecules. The disease is most commonly caused by a point mutation within the TTR gene inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion. Over 100 of such mutations have been identified, leading to destabilization of the physiological TTR tetramer. As a result, many monomers originate with a tendency for spontaneous conformational changes and self-aggregation.
